title: Shift normalization of canonical ringed-slice comparisons
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous and define a morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits. Let $R$ on $\mathcal D$ and $S$ on $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative rings with a specified isomorphism $f^{-1}R\cong S$. For $V\in\mathcal D$ put $U=u(V)$, use the restricted rings on the slice sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and let $f_V$ be the induced ringed morphism [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\beta_E:j_V^*Rf_*E\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*E$ and $\theta_P:Lf_V^*j_V^*P\cong j_U^*Lf^*P$ be the canonical, derived-adjunction-compatible comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], and let $\tau_{M,N}:j_V^*(M\otimes_R^LN)\cong j_V^*M\otimes_{R|_V}^Lj_V^*N$ be the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; also use the corresponding tensor comparison for $j_U^*$. Then $\beta$, $\theta$, and both tensor comparisons commute with the canonical integer-shift isomorphisms in each input. Precisely, for each comparison $c:F\cong G$ and each input shifted by $n\in\mathbf Z$, $s_G c_{[n]}=c[n]s_F$, with the other inputs fixed. The unary shift is $(K[n])^r=K^{r+n}$ with differential $(-1)^nd_K$. For the total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the shift map $A[n]\otimes B\cong(A\otimes B)[n]$ is identity on summands and $A\otimes B[n]\cong(A\otimes B)[n]$ multiplies the summand of first degree $p$ by $(-1)^{np}$. The derived pullback and pushforward shifts are those obtained by shifting their resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift].
